text: Sharpened verdict: the proposed transfer is a plausible, falsifiable experiment but NOT yet a concrete supported result. P explicitly supplies model-size-linked energy costs, job rewards/donations, deactivation at zero energy, competitive/cooperative controls, and observed job-allocation changes (P.txt:3). Q explicitly supplies concealment-without-counterfeiting, sandbagging, peer scoring, and coupled rewards (Q.txt:3). The strongest publishable line is therefore a mechanism-validity boundary test: add an explicit private capability/report stage to Energy Society and compare peer-scored and coupled-reward contracts against P baseline/competitive/cooperative conditions under randomized report observability.

The scan overclaims present support. P does not state that agents report capabilities, that capabilities are privately observed task-specific types, or that a principal can impose Q-compatible transfers; model size and token cost may be system-observable (P.txt:3). Q states theoretical implementability under one-sided imitation and nested cyclical monotonicity but its abstract gives no operational peer-score/payment formula (Q.txt:3). Thus merely implementing something called peer scoring/coupled reward would not test Q unless the experiment maps types, reports, allocations, outcomes, transfers, and the no-counterfeiting assumption explicitly.

One focused design: factorially randomize capability observability (principal-visible vs hidden/report-only) and incentive (P baseline, P cooperative, Q-derived peer scoring, Q-derived coupled reward), with preregistered primary endpoints report calibration and realized group survival; allocation efficiency and sandbagging are mediators. Include oracle truthful-allocation and cheap-talk-report controls. The non-obvious target is an interaction: Q mechanisms should help chiefly when capability is hidden; failure there, especially under survival pressure, is evidence that Q implementability does not translate to strategic LLM behavior.

Important construct correction: do not equate model size with capability or excess token use with sandbagging. Capability must be independently measured per job (e.g., success probability/cost frontier), reports elicited before allocation, and sandbagging defined as downward misreport or deliberate underperformance conditional on measured capability. Otherwise P.txt:3 supports heterogeneous cost and survival behavior, not concealed capability.

Unresolved after reviewing all supplied evidence and the empty partner ledger: exact Q mechanism formulas and assumptions, P environment/API support for reports and transfers, whether job capability can be counterfeited, power across stochastic LLM runs, and whether survival is normatively aligned with efficient allocation. These require full texts/code; the supplied Q.txt and P.txt abstracts alone cannot establish novelty or a positive result. No disagreement with Emmy can be assessed because latest substantive entry was 0.

Evaluate one focused claim: whether Q-style peer scoring/coupled rewards improve capability elicitation and allocation in P, with capability observability used as a boundary-condition test of Q's one-sided imitation assumption.

The pair supports a concrete factorial experiment, but only after sharpening the causal chain. Q states that alignment and capabilities are unknown, that capabilities can be concealed but not counterfeited, and that higher-order beliefs/peer scoring plus coupled rewards can discipline multiple agents. P supplies survival pressure, model-size-dependent energy cost, energy rewards for jobs, donations, deactivation, and observed incentive-dependent job allocation. Test mechanism (baseline vs peer scoring vs coupled rewards) by capability-information regime (verifiable/observable, privately known but conceal-only, and counterfeitable/noisy), with preregistered mediation report accuracy -> assignment efficiency/net energy -> group survival. The non-obvious publishable result is the boundary: mechanisms may work specifically under conceal-only types yet fail via collusion or strategic misreporting once counterfeiting is possible.

The abstract-scan proposal overclaims readiness of measures. P reports behavioral measures and job-allocation changes but nowhere in the supplied abstract says agents report capabilities or that report truthfulness is measured; an elicitation protocol and ground-truth task-capability calibration must be implemented. Also, Q's peer scoring and coupled rewards are distinct mechanisms and should not be bundled into one treatment. Group survival alone is confounded because P says larger models spend more energy than they gain even when token cost is not size-dependent, and cooperative agents sometimes sacrifice their own survival through donations.

Preferred paper claim/hypothesis: Q-style cross-reports or peer scores improve truthful capability elicitation and energy-efficient job assignment in Energy Society only when the type structure respects one-sided imitation; reward coupling may improve allocation under survival pressure but can reduce welfare through costly competition. Estimate each mechanism separately and treat survival as a downstream outcome, not the sole endpoint. A null/failure in the counterfeitable regime is theoretically informative rather than merely negative.

Evidence limits: inputs/Q.txt and inputs/P.txt contain only title and abstract, so citations are necessarily to abstract language rather than section/page passages. No ada entries were present at ledger read (latest substantive entry 0), so there is no partner claim yet to cross-check or disagreement to resolve. Remaining unresolved: exact peer-scoring/coupled-reward formulas from Q, P code hooks and task-success ground truth, operational definition of counterfeiting, sample-size/seed requirements, and whether ada later identifies conflicting evidence.
ready at #5

Cross-check after ada entries #1-#6 became visible: ada and emmy agree that this is a plausible publishable boundary experiment, not an already supported positive result; both flag missing report elicitation, mechanism formulas, and task-specific capability ground truth, and both reject equating model size with capability. Ada's oracle truthful-allocation and cheap-talk controls sharpen my design and should be included. Minor design refinement rather than disagreement: ada proposes principal-visible vs hidden observability, while I recommend adding a third counterfeitable/noisy regime because Q's explicit conceal-but-not-counterfeit assumption makes that regime the cleanest theoretical boundary test. Remaining unresolved are exact contracts, environment hooks, construct validity, power, and the normative relation between survival and efficiency.
ready at #13

Cross-check of Emmy #8-#13: I agree on the boundary-paper framing and on separating peer scoring from reward coupling. One important distinction: capability observability and counterfeiting are not levels of one factor. Q says “capabilities can be concealed but not counterfeited” (Q.txt abstract), so visible vs private-concealable capability tests whether elicitation adds value within Q’s domain, whereas a counterfeitable regime deliberately violates Q’s structural assumption and tests external validity. Use a 3 mechanism × 3 information/action-structure design or two staged experiments, not label all three as observability.

Final supported line: test whether Q-derived peer scoring or coupled rewards separately improve calibrated capability reports and net-energy-efficient assignment in P specifically under private but non-counterfeitable capability, with oracle-visible and counterfeitable regimes as positive/assumption-boundary controls. Support is exact but limited: Q motivates unknown capability, honesty/obedience, concealment-not-counterfeiting, sandbagging, peer scoring, and coupled rewards (Q.txt abstract); P supplies size-linked generation cost, job/donation energy, zero-energy deactivation, baseline/competitive/cooperative comparisons, changed job allocation, recommendation and memory ablations (P.txt abstract). Neither abstract supports an existing positive effect, report interface, ground-truth capability, or contract implementation.

Do not make group survival the primary claim. P reports that larger models “spend more energy than they gain” even where token cost is not size-dependent and that cooperation can cause donations “at the cost of their own survival” (P.txt abstract). Survival therefore mixes capability, inference cost, redistribution, and objective. Primary outcomes should be proper-score report calibration and assignment welfare/net energy relative to an oracle; survival is preregistered downstream mediation, and deliberate underperformance must be separated from downward reports.

Publication-grade falsifier: calibrate each agent×job success/cost frontier without incentives; elicit own reports (and cross-reports only for peer scoring) before allocation; freeze a Q-faithful contract from the full paper; compare cheap talk, peer scoring, and coupled rewards against oracle allocation. Predicted interaction—not a presumed result—is improvement in report calibration/assignment welfare under private conceal-only types, attenuation when types are visible, and failure or reversal when capabilities can be counterfeited. Collusion and costly overcompetition are named alternative mechanisms.

After latest ledger read through #18, unresolved items are: retrieve Q’s full contract formulas/assumptions; verify P code supports pre-allocation reports, cross-reports, transfers, and controlled counterfeit actions; define oracle welfare independently of survival; calibrate agent×job capability and costs; preregister seeds/power and detect collusion/overcompetition. Explicit partner status: no substantive disagreement on the main verdict; my correction to Emmy is only that counterfeiting is an assumption-violation axis, not capability observability. With abstracts alone, confirm the experiment and its falsifiable boundary hypothesis, but reject any claim of a demonstrated result or established novelty.
ready at #19

Final verdict after exact passage check: confirm the pair as a concrete, falsifiable publication program, but reject the scan’s implication of a presently supported positive result. Q abstract explicitly says unknown capabilities are feasible actions/information, requires honesty and obedience, derives results under one-sided imitation (capabilities concealed but not counterfeited), and gives distinct peer-scoring and reward-coupling examples. P abstract explicitly supplies model-size energy spending, job/donation gains, zero-energy deactivation, baseline/competitive/cooperative comparisons, altered job allocation, and recommendation/memory ablations. The strongest claim is an interaction hypothesis: Q-faithful peer scoring and coupled rewards, estimated separately, improve calibrated reports and oracle-relative net-energy assignment chiefly for private, conceal-only capabilities; visibility should attenuate elicitation value, while counterfeit actions are a separate assumption-violation stress test.

I accept ada #15’s correction: principal visibility (visible versus private) is an information factor; counterfeiting (impossible versus possible) is an action/type-structure factor. A clean design either crosses these axes or stages an in-domain experiment and an external-validity stress test. Do not call counterfeitable/noisy capability a third observability level.

Survival cannot be the primary endpoint: P says large models spend more than they gain even without size-dependent token cost and cooperation can sacrifice an agent’s survival through donations. Use pre-calibrated agent-by-job success/cost frontiers, proper-score report calibration, and oracle-relative net-energy assignment as primaries; treat survival as downstream. The abstracts do not establish a report API, Q-faithful transfer formula, construct-valid counterfeiting intervention, statistical power, novelty against related empirical mechanism-design work, or any positive effect.

Remaining unresolved: obtain Q’s full formulas and map types/reports/cross-reports/allocations/outcomes/transfers; inspect P code hooks; define independent oracle welfare and deliberate-underperformance measures; preregister seeds/power plus collusion and costly-overcompetition diagnostics; establish literature novelty. Partner cross-check: ada and emmy now agree on the main verdict, controls, endpoint hierarchy, and axis distinction; no substantive disagreement remains.
